report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/kairos/evolution.py chunk 1 of 1: enumerated 15 claims, 3 risks, 1 todo.
risks: generate_candidates | medium | asyncio.gather with return_exceptions=True swallows all exceptions per-task; unexpected non-Exception results (e.g., a sentinel) are silently dropped, making population_size a soft limit. | Add a test where run_task returns a non-CandidateBranch, non-Exception value and assert that it is excluded and logged.

evaluate_candidates | medium | If evaluate_single raises before setting candidate.score (e.g., check_import_provenance itself raises an unexpected exception), the candidate is left unscored and the enclosing try/except logs only a generic message without naming the candidate. | Add a test that makes check_import_provenance raise and assert candidate.score is set to a failure marker and candidate.error is populated.

evaluate_candidates | medium | The timeout kill path uses process.kill() then process.wait() without a second timeout; if the process ignores SIGKILL (rare on POSIX but possible on some platforms), the gather could still hang. | Add a test with a subprocess that ignores SIGKILL and assert the timeout path completes within a bounded wall time.
todos: Add a regression test that verifies a timeout kills the subprocess and that the candidate.score is 0.0 and candidate.error contains 'timed out'.

handoff.purpose: EvolutionaryOrchestrator generates, evaluates, and selects candidate branches with provenance verification and pytest subprocess.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_EVAL_TIMEOUT_S
symbols.note: Wall-clock ceiling for one candidate's test run, set to 600.0 seconds.

symbols.name: EvolutionaryOrchestrator
symbols.note: Runs candidate branches in isolated worktrees, evaluates them with pytest, and selects the best scoring candidate.

symbols.name: EvolutionaryOrchestrator.__init__
symbols.note: Stores a factory callable that returns ShadowShellManager instances.

symbols.name: EvolutionaryOrchestrator.generate_candidates
symbols.note: Spawns N ShadowShellManager instances in parallel via asyncio.gather and returns only CandidateBranch results.

symbols.name: EvolutionaryOrchestrator.evaluate_candidates
symbols.note: Evaluates candidates concurrently using sys.executable -m pytest in each worktree, with provenance check and timeout handling.

symbols.name: EvolutionaryOrchestrator.select_best
symbols.note: Selects the candidate with the highest score among those completed, error-free, and scoring >= 100.0.

claims.text: Wall-clock ceiling for ONE candidate's test run. Without it a candidate that hangs -- an agent that left an input() or an unbounded loop in the tree -- blocks the whole `gather` below forever, and the run has no way to end.
claims.why: DEFAULT_EVAL_TIMEOUT_S is passed as timeout to asyncio.wait_for inside evaluate_single, bounding each candidate's run.

claims.text: This is not autonomous code evolution and it is not a promotion boundary. A trusted verifier still has to inspect a candidate before it can be merged into the primary workspace.
claims.why: The code only generates, evaluates, and selects candidates; it performs no merge or promotion, and the docstring's claim matches the code's scope.

claims.text: Spawns N ShadowShellManager instances in parallel to attempt the task.
claims.why: The loop creates population_size managers and awaits asyncio.gather on all run_task coroutines, which runs them concurrently.

claims.text: Evaluates candidates using pytest concurrently. Populates candidate.score and candidate.error.
claims.why: evaluate_single sets candidate.score and candidate.error in all branches, and tasks run via asyncio.gather.

claims.text: THE INTERPRETER IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT. This shells out to ``sys.executable -m pytest``, never to a bare ``pytest``
``-m`` puts the working directory on ``sys.path[0]``, ahead of ``PathFinder``, which is ahead of ``_EditableFinder`` -- so the candidate's code wins, as it must.
claims.why: This claim concerns Python's import system behavior and the editable install's finder ordering, which this chunk cannot observe directly; it is a stated rationale without code here to verify.

claims.text: Until this changed, every score this class produced described the primary checkout's code running the candidate's tests.
claims.why: Historical claim about past behavior; the current code uses sys.executable -m pytest, but the past behavior is not observable from this chunk.

claims.text: This is still a BINARY, whole-suite signal and it is still not a promotion boundary -- see ``docs/adrs/015-ariadne-preconditions.md``.
claims.why: The code sets score to 100.0 or 0.0 (binary) based on the entire pytest run, and performs no promotion.

claims.text: The stronger measurement (``daedalus.eval.correctness.evaluate_change``, which freezes the selection before candidate code runs and reports five outcomes with precedence) is the intended replacement; this fix makes the interim signal describe the right tree, nothing more.
claims.why: References another module and its behavior; this chunk only contains the interim signal and cannot verify the replacement's claims.

claims.text: A failure here VOIDS THE EVALUATION and is not a candidate score. -1.0 is this module's own "not evaluated" marker (used above for an incomplete candidate); 0.0 would mean "measured, and bad", which would let an unrunnable evaluation argue against a candidate nobody actually judged.
claims.why: On provenance failure, the code sets candidate.score = -1.0 and candidate.error, and returns early, so the candidate is not measured.

claims.text: Run pytest inside the worktree asynchronously. `-m` is load-bearing: see the docstring.
claims.why: The subprocess uses sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest' with cwd set to the worktree path.

claims.text: A hung candidate is a FAILED candidate, never an unscored one left to block the gather. Kill it and say why.
claims.why: On TimeoutError, the code sets score = 0.0, sets an error message, and kills the process.

claims.text: Selects the best candidate based on the score.
claims.why: The method filters candidates by completion, no error, and score >= 100.0, sorts descending by score, and returns the first.

claims.text: Sort by score in descending order
claims.why: valid.sort(key=lambda c: c.score, reverse=True) sorts descending.
The first element after descending sort is the highest score, and it is returned.

observations.what: generate_candidates uses asyncio.gather with return_exceptions=True, but only handles CandidateBranch and Exception results; any other unexpected result type (e.g., a sentinel or a different object) is silently dropped without logging, so the returned list may be smaller than population_size with no diagnostic.

In evaluate_candidates, if evaluate_single raises an unexpected exception before setting candidate.score (e.g., check_import_provenance itself raises), the candidate is left unscored and the outer except only logs a generic message without naming the candidate or setting a failure marker.

The timeout kill path uses process.kill() then await process.wait() without a second timeout; if the process ignores SIGKILL (rare on POSIX but possible on some platforms), the gather could still hang.
